events.title: c64-disk: sectors writes the 256 bytes of the given sectors, then with --unreferenced each used sector that no file holds, into one file and gives the track, sector and offset of each; before, bam listed the unreferenced sectors but nothing read their bytes, and bam now names this command as its nextAction when such sectors exist
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-testing: a record file can say where the coverage of the recording starts, with "coverage": "input" (the default, at the first input read of code in RAM), "start" (when the program starts) or a $ address (at its first execution, also at the pc of a registers step), and the record summary gives coverageFrom with the frame and pc where the map starts, or null, because a map that started after the start-up code made an agent think that game_start and its writes did not run; c64run protocol 3 adds coverage on-pc and coverage status
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: An analyzer reference from a data region of the user, the LLM or a heuristic is false code from packed bytes that the analyzer decoded: the import drops it and counts it in references.inData, the analyzer's own reference from there closes also in a run that is not complete, and a classify of data closes the analyzer references from its range; dual-use bytes keep theirs; before, such references stayed in reference pages and reachability and came back on each run
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: A trace of thousands of hits reaches the caller: the hits go as an attachment of the reply, not in the one message that holds at most 1 MiB, and a result too large for one reply gets limit-exceeded with its size and a remedy and a host log line, not a generic operation-failed; hello and ready also carry the package version, so a client and a host of different releases refuse the handshake and name the older side (a development checkout passes against any release), the protocol version is 5, and after a lost session the MCP server gives that refusal instead of the stored machine-state-lost notice
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-source: a read or a write in the I/O area names the register also where the image holds RAM there (lda CI2CRA, sta RASTER, sta $d800,x for colour RAM without a name, not an offset of the data label at $d000), a platform name in a knowledge operand expression stays as written and becomes a constant in constants.asm, and the RAM keeps its data label without a platform-name label, because a game that copies sprites under the I/O area got every register access written as region+offset; a user or LLM name at the address still wins
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-assembler: an include folder can be anywhere in the project folder, for example build src boot.asm --include ../build for a file that you generated next to the source root: the script stages only the source root and the include folders from the lowest folder that holds them, ACME runs in the source root inside that tree, a diagnostic in such a folder names the file from the source root (../build/tables.asm), and a folder outside the project is refused by name; before, a path with .. was refused and the project folder had to be the source root, which staged the whole project
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-provenance: match keeps the overlapping copies of a routine and names a routine with several copies only at the copy that has the shift of its nearest library neighbours that occur once, or at no copy with an ambiguous reason for each, because the lowest copy was often the wrong one; a $xxxx address in a library comment inside the routine moves by the shift of the match, and a written comment with an address outside the routine is in batch.check for the agent to examine
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-testing: a run file and a scenario name a missing or wrong field with its form (name is a non-empty string, start is a program, a program with load or a snapshot, original and rebuild have program and symbols) and refuse a key that they do not have with the list of their keys, and the run help, SKILL.md and the format reference give the required and optional fields of a run file, because a run file without name failed with "needs a name" and the help did not tell that name is required
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-source: the export rewrite of a scenario gives each side only program and symbols, because a scenario now refuses any other key in original and rebuild and a copied videoStandard made the rewritten scenario fail
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-source: when the check of loader.prg cannot run (the emulator is not available, or another refusal), generate --loader removes the loader.prg that it wrote and gives the normal result with loader.verified false and the reason, and a run without --loader that keeps a loader.asm of another knowledge revision gives staleLoader with the files and a generate --loader nextAction, because an unchecked or stale loader.prg looked like a checked one and a failed check lost the list of written files
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: An overdue binary-monitor request whose answer never comes no longer caps every later request at the short overdue time limit: VICE answers in order, so the answer to a later request clears each overdue request sent before it, and slow commands such as memmap, hunt, step and snapshot get their full time limit again after VICE goes on
events.author: Henrik Olsson

DM1 Amiga v2.0 completed all five title fades in a measured 1,698 ms (366 ms zoom, 500 ms hold, 166 ms final fade); headless checks also cover DM1, CSB and DM2 startup. This is a verified configuration, not a minimum CPU/RAM, HiDPI, pixel-parity, beam-timing or audible-speaker claim. v3.0.397 additionally records authentic five-game scan times of 27.90 s cold and 12.35 s warm on this host; other hosts remain unmeasured.

before.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
before.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

before.name: Swift64 v0.4.2 Apple Silicon application
before.notes: The universal release was packaged and run to BASIC READY on Apple Silicon. User-supplied BASIC, KERNAL and character ROMs are required; 1541 media/ROM support varies by mode. No CPU-generation or RAM minimum is stated.

before.name: Swift64 v0.4.2 Intel application slice
before.notes: The universal release explicitly includes an Intel binary, but upstream labels it build-verified rather than runtime-tested. User-supplied ROMs are required; no CPU-generation or RAM minimum is stated.

after.name: Swift64 v0.6.0 Apple Silicon application
after.notes: The universal release was packaged and run to BASIC READY on Apple Silicon. User-supplied BASIC, KERNAL and character ROMs are required; 1541 media/ROM support varies by mode. No CPU-generation or RAM minimum is stated.

after.notes: The universal release explicitly includes an Intel binary, but upstream labels it build-verified rather than runtime-tested. User-supplied ROMs are required; no CPU-generation or RAM minimum is stated.

before.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
before.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

after.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
after.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

before.name: Swift64 macOS application
before.notes: README and Package.swift explicitly require macOS 14+. User-supplied BASIC, KERNAL and character ROMs are needed; 1541 ROM is optional for fast-load but required for true-drive mode. No host ISA/RAM minimum or broad game compatibility is established.

after.notes: The universal release was packaged and run to BASIC READY on Apple Silicon. User-supplied BASIC, KERNAL and character ROMs are required; 1541 media/ROM support varies by mode. No CPU-generation or RAM minimum is stated.

after.name: Swift64 v0.4.2 Intel application slice
after.notes: The universal release explicitly includes an Intel binary, but upstream labels it build-verified rather than runtime-tested. User-supplied ROMs are required; no CPU-generation or RAM minimum is stated.

before.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
before.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification.

after.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
after.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

change_details.after: v1.10.2 stable source SDK released; optional Q8 experiments remain emulator-qualified and physical hardware remains untested

before.name: A1200 release
before.notes: Author specifies Amiga 1200 or WinUAE configured as one. Fast RAM recommended but not required for release; debug executable requires fast RAM. Three original game disks required.

after.name: A1200 release
after.notes: Author specifies Amiga 1200 or WinUAE configured as one: 68020, AGA, Kickstart 3.x and 2 MiB chip RAM. Fast RAM is recommended but not required for release; debug requires fast RAM. Three original game disks are required. Network play additionally needs bsdsocket.library from WinUAE or an Amiga TCP/IP stack.

change_details.before: Upstream-reported playable A1200 reconstruction; original disks required; public-build proof documented.
change_details.after: v0.2.0 Amiga HD release; playable A1200 reconstruction with local/network co-op; Windows SDL port in progress

events.title: Project metadata updated

before.name: MEGA65 R6 (upstream-tested beta)
before.notes: README explicitly reports 0.4.7 beta tested on a real R6. Requires the board’s SDRAM, SD card, tos.img and user media. R4/R5 projects are advertised but explicitly untested; R3/R3A are unsupported. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is used as a host CPU/RAM minimum.

after.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R6
after.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum.

after.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
after.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

change_details.before: 0.4.7 beta; author-tested on MEGA65 R6, further hardware modes untested
change_details.after: v1.0 stable; upstream-tested on MEGA65 R6 and R3A; R4/R5 untested

events.title: New options --cmt <file>, --cmt-play, --cmt-play-pause and --cmt-boot: insert a tape (MZF, MZT, TAP or WAV) into the virtual cassette recorder at startup. The CMT hack is turned off for that session only and the Virtual CMT window opens. --cmt-play presses PLAY, --cmt-play-pause leaves the tape waiting until the computer turns the cassette motor on, and --cmt-boot (MZ-800) also holds the C key at startup so the boot menu loads the program from the tape.

events.title: BUGFIX: CTC 8253 - a counter loaded the written value depending on when the control word came instead of on the phase of its CLK input. Measured on a real MZ-800, the value is loaded by the first complete CLK pulse after the write: written while CLK is HIGH it loads one pulse later than written while CLK is LOW, the time of the control word does not matter. The CTC2 interrupt (clocked by CTC1) therefore came one CTC1 period earlier or later than on the real computer in some programs. Mode 0 now reads 0000h for a whole CLK period after reaching zero (previously FFFFh at once). Mode 3 reads the counter in steps of 2 like the real chip (previously 1); with an odd N the first half period of the output (HIGH) is the longer one, the tone frequency does not change.

events.title: DOCS FIX: MCP - the memory banking description (emulator://docs/memory_layout) claimed that IORQ OUT does not change the CG-ROM mapping on the MZ-800; in fact OUT (0E0h) unmaps the CG-ROM too (the VRAM stays) and OUT (0E4h) maps it together with the VRAM in MZ-800 mode and unmaps it together with the CG-RAM in MZ-700 mode. The pair IN A,(0E0h) + OUT (0E0h),A therefore gives RAM at 0000h-1FFFh and the VRAM at the same time. The emulator already behaved this way.

change_details.before: Amiga Games — Dot Chase, Fractalus and Void Trader collection
change_details.after: Amiga Games — native games and 3DO-derived AmigaOS ports

before.name: Dot Chase: selected classic 68k build
before.notes: -m68020 build with intuition.library and graphics.library v39, four-plane LORES screen. No PPC branch is evidenced. RAM and chipset minima are unstated; not independently run.

before.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: selected classic AGA builds
before.notes: Both selected builds use -m68020, explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp and v39 OS libraries. No minimum RAM or measured performance threshold is established. 64 KiB stack requests are not RAM minima.

before.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: PPC OS4 variants
before.notes: ARCH=ppc selects -mcpu=440 and newlib with sam460ex/QEMU intent. The PPC variants use silent audio stubs; Fractalus uses graphics.library fallback rendering. Pacing/freezing limitations are author-reported. This does not cover Dot Chase or the whole collection; exact CPU/RAM minimum remains unverified.

after.name: Dot Chase: selected classic 68k build
after.notes: -m68020 build with intuition.library and graphics.library v39, four-plane LORES screen. No PPC branch is evidenced. RAM and chipset minima are unstated; not independently run.

after.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: selected classic AGA builds
after.notes: Both selected builds use -m68020, explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp and v39 OS libraries. No minimum RAM or measured performance threshold is established. 64 KiB stack requests are not RAM minima.

after.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: PPC OS4 variants
after.notes: ARCH=ppc selects -mcpu=440 and newlib with sam460ex/QEMU intent. The PPC variants use silent audio stubs; Fractalus uses graphics.library fallback rendering. Pacing/freezing limitations are author-reported. This does not cover Dot Chase or the whole collection; exact CPU/RAM minimum remains unverified.

after.name: Planet Chomp, Rolling Steel and Spectral Keep: PPC OS4 source ports
after.notes: The three source-level ports are PPC-only and build with ppc-amigaos-gcc -mcpu=440fp/newlib. Planet Chomp and Rolling Steel use OSMesa 7.8.2 software rendering; Spectral Keep renders its precomputed sprites in software. Upstream reports QEMU sam460ex performance, but no minimum physical CPU or RAM requirement is established.

change_details.before: Three substantive game anchors reviewed; per-game 68k/PPC variants and parent-library dependency; independently untested
change_details.after: Six substantive game anchors reviewed across classic 68k and PPC AmigaOS variants; independently unbuilt

before.name: Mode 7 Q8 fast accelerated-emulation qualification
before.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz and measured the public rotating cube with Turbo6510 at 64 MHz: 6.95 PAL / 7.25 NTSC views per second for the fast profile versus 3.10 / 3.20 for standard. This is scene-specific emulator evidence, not a minimum, an 8-FPS guarantee or physical-hardware qualification.

after.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
after.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification.

events.title: BUGFIX: MCP - emu_media_run_mzf only loaded the program and jumped to its start; interrupt mode, Z80 PIO, CTC, palette and all other state stayed as the previous program left them, so the program could behave differently than after a tape load (e.g. it got no interrupts). It now resets the machine and starts the program in the same state as the --run-mzf option (new command media_run_mzf). A missing or truncated file returns an error without a reset. The old behaviour without a reset is available as emu_media_run_mzf with bootstrap=false.

before.name: Default OCS build
before.os: Kickstart 1.3; Workbench 1.3 or later for icon launch
before.notes: The documented baseline is PAL OCS with 512 KB Chip RAM plus 512 KB expansion RAM. The delivered image runs on a stock MC68000 and switches to wider routines automatically on 68020+ CPUs.

evidence.excerpt: Target: PAL OCS, MC68000, Kickstart 1.3, 512 KB Chip RAM plus 512 KB expansion RAM.
Double-click it to launch the game from Workbench 1.3 or later.

before.name: 68020-only build
before.notes: The explicit cpu=68020 build assembles only the native 68020 forms. The README does not restate a separate RAM minimum for this variant, so RAM is left unspecified.

evidence.excerpt: cpu=68020 still assembles the native forms only, for a tighter image that needs an MC68020.

after.name: Enhanced Atari ST build
after.notes: The root README describes the enhanced Atari ST MC68000 build and Atari floppy/TOS distribution. No minimum RAM is stated here.

evidence.excerpt: Buildable Elite sources for the MC68000: the enhanced Atari ST version in src_atari, a separate native Amiga port in src_amiga, and the preserved original Atari ST version in src_orig.

events.title: Project metadata updated

before.name: Atari ST / STE / Mega ST 68000 build
before.notes: The shipping ST/STE binary is compiled for a bare 68000 and is explicitly described as the safe run-on-anything Atari build; a stock non-e ST is verified.

evidence.excerpt: Atari ST / STE / Mega ST — openua-atari-st-*.zip, 2 MB, colour monitor; tested on TOS 2.06, EmuTOS and TOS 1.04.
A 68000 build runs on any Atari, and a stock non-e ST is verified too.

before.name: Atari Falcon / TT 020-60 build
before.notes: The Falcon/TT binary uses -m68020-60 code generation; the same binary may also be used on an accelerated ST/STE with a 68020 or better.

evidence.excerpt: Atari Falcon030 / TT030 — openua-falcon-*.zip, 4 MB, TOS 4.04 (Falcon) or 3.0x (TT).
The Falcon/TT zip is -m68020-60; requirements are an 020 or better.

before.name: Amiga ECS/OCS
before.notes: Bare-68000 ECS/OCS build; Kickstart 1.3 will not launch it. The documentation describes 7 MHz as playable, with acceleration improving comfort.

evidence.excerpt: Amiga ECS/OCS (A500+ / A600 / A2000, bare 68000) — Kickstart 2.0 or later, 2 MB; playable at 7 MHz.

before.name: Amiga AGA / RTG
before.notes: One binary serves AGA and Picasso96/CyberGraphX RTG, selecting the display path at runtime; the AGA path is documented for A1200/A4000-class machines.

evidence.excerpt: Amiga AGA (A1200 / A4000) and RTG — Kickstart 3.0+, about 4 MB; one frua serves AGA and Picasso96/CyberGraphX RTG.
The codebase is already GCC -std=gnu99 -m68020 C.

after.name: Atari ST / STE / Mega ST 68000 build
after.notes: The shipping ST/STE binary is compiled for a bare 68000 and is explicitly described as the safe run-on-anything Atari build; a stock non-e ST is verified.

evidence.excerpt: Atari ST / STE / Mega ST — openua-atari-st-*.zip, 2 MB, colour monitor; tested on TOS 2.06, EmuTOS and TOS 1.04.
A 68000 build runs on any Atari, and a stock non-e ST is verified too.

after.name: Atari Falcon030 / TT030
after.notes: One -m68020-60 binary serves both Falcon030 and TT030; the standard target machines documented here are 68030 systems.

evidence.excerpt: Atari Falcon030 / TT030 — openua-falcon-*.zip, 4 MB, TOS 4.04 (Falcon) or 3.0x (TT). One binary serves both.
The Macintosh 68k code is retargeted to machines including the target 68020/030 family; Falcon030 and TT030 are supported backends.

after.name: Accelerated Atari ST / STE 020+ build
after.os: No extra TOS floor documented; TOS 2.06 tested
after.notes: On an accelerated ST/STE the Falcon/TT -m68020-60 binary detects ST hardware and selects the native ST display backend. The documentation explicitly states an 020 or better is required for this variant.

evidence.excerpt: Run the Falcon/TT zip's binary; the Falcon/TT zip is -m68020-60. Requirements are just the accelerator: an 020 or better.

after.name: Amiga ECS/OCS
after.notes: Bare-68000 ECS/OCS build; Kickstart 1.3 will not launch it. The documentation describes 7 MHz as playable, with acceleration improving comfort.

evidence.excerpt: Amiga ECS/OCS (A500+ / A600 / A2000, bare 68000) — Kickstart 2.0 or later, 2 MB; playable at 7 MHz.

after.name: Amiga AGA / RTG
after.notes: One -m68020 Amiga binary serves AGA and Picasso96/CyberGraphX RTG, selecting the display path at runtime. The hardware guide describes memory as about 4 MB, so no exact minimum RAM value is asserted here.

evidence.excerpt: Amiga AGA (A1200 / A4000) and RTG — Kickstart 3.0+, about 4 MB; one frua serves AGA and Picasso96/CyberGraphX RTG.
The codebase is already GCC -std=gnu99 -m68020 C.
